item.title: Trump diz que visitará no Texas petroleiro com primeiro petróleo de acordo com Venezuela
item.description: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta terça-feira que planeja visitar um navio-tanque no Texas que contém o primeiro petróleo recebido da Venezuela, após um acordo firmado por Washington depois da destituição do ex-líder do país.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou nesta terça-feira que planeja visitar um navio-tanque no Texas que contém o primeiro petróleo recebido da Venezuela, após um acordo firmado por Washington depois da destituição do ex-líder do país. Trump anunciou em agosto um acordo que concede aos Estados Unidos acesso a um quinto das reservas de petróleo bruto da Venezuela. “Eles me enviaram, como presente, um carregamento de um milhão de barris de petróleo, e vou entregar isso aos Estados Unidos da América”, disse Trump aos repórteres. Mais tarde, ele afirmou em uma postagem no Truth Social que essa era a “primeira remessa de BILHÕES de barris que estão por vir”. A Casa Branca informou em setembro que o petróleo proveniente do acordo com a Venezuela provavelmente chegaria às reservas dos EUA em novembro. Os Estados Unidos vêm trabalhando em estreita colaboração com o governo interino liderado pela presidente interina, Delcy Rodríguez, desde que forças americanas capturaram o então presidente Nicolás Maduro em janeiro.

item.title: Oracle amplía su acuerdo de suministro de chips con Nvidia e incorpora la oferta de Google y Cerebras
item.description: Oracle anunció el martes que está ampliando sus acuerdos sobre chips de IA en la nube con Nvidia, al tiempo que diversifica su oferta para incluir productos de competidores de Nvidia, como Google, de Alphabet , y Cerebras Systems.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: Oracle anunció el martes que está ampliando sus acuerdos sobre chips de IA en la nube con Nvidia, al tiempo que diversifica su oferta para incluir productos de competidores de Nvidia, como Google, de Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , y Cerebras Systems. Oracle (ORCL.N) y Nvidia (NVDA.O) dijeron que la empresa de servicios en la nube se expandirá a una "escala de varios gigavatios" con la última generación de servidores de IA "Vera Rubin" de Nvidia. Las empresas no revelaron el valor del acuerdo, aunque el director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, había declarado anteriormente que los sistemas Vera Rubin pueden generar hasta 40.000 millones de dólares en ingresos por gigavatio para el fabricante de chips. Oracle también está diversificando su oferta y ha señalado que incluso los sistemas basados en Nvidia prescindirán de algunos de los chips de red de Nvidia en favor de los chips de red "Acceleron", desarrollados internamente por Oracle. El martes, Oracle anunció que comenzará a ofrecer por primera vez los chips de unidad de procesamiento tensorial (TPU) de Google. "Las diferentes cargas de trabajo de IA tienen distintas necesidades de computación", afirmó Mahesh Thiagarajan, presidente de Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, en un comunicado. "Esa opción ofrece a los clientes la flexibilidad de elegir la infraestructura adecuada en función del rendimiento, la productividad y la rentabilidad de cada carga de trabajo de IA". Además de los chips de Google, Oracle tiene previsto ofrecer chips de SambaNova Systems y Cerebras Systems (CBRS.O) , dos empresas respaldadas por Intel (INTC.O) , que fabrican chips para lo que se conoce como "inferencia", es decir, cuando los sistemas de IA responden a las solicitudes de los usuarios humanos. Mientras que Nvidia domina el mercado del entrenamiento de sistemas de IA, el mercado de la inferencia es más competitivo y diverso. "Se trata de una expansión masiva de nuestra base de clientes de primer nivel", dijo el director ejecutivo de Cerebras, Andrew Feldman, sobre el acuerdo con Oracle en una entrevista con Reuters. "Nos están implementando a gran escala en los centros de datos de terceros". Oracle, que tiene previsto celebrar esta semana una jornada para inversores, no ha revelado cómo piensa financiar la compra de los chips. Durante una conferencia sobre resultados celebrada el mes pasado, Oracle señaló que los clientes asumen cada vez más el costo de los chips y mantuvo su objetivo de gasto de capital de entre 90.000 y 95.000 millones de dólares para el ejercicio fiscal de 2027.

item.title: Bolsas europeas no sufren por flojo desempeño de HSBC, otros resultados mejoran ánimo inversores
item.description: Los buenos resultados empresariales y la baja del petróleo contribuyeron a que las acciones europeas cerraran al alza el martes, compensando las pérdidas registradas a primera hora de la sesión, cuando HSBC lastró el ánimo de los inversores tras no alcanzar los ingresos trimestrales previstos.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: Los buenos resultados empresariales y la baja del petróleo contribuyeron a que las acciones europeas cerraran al alza el martes, compensando las pérdidas registradas a primera hora de la sesión, cuando HSBC lastró el ánimo de los inversores tras no alcanzar los ingresos trimestrales previstos. El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) subió un 0,47% a 643,68 puntos, tras haber llegado a caer un 0,41% a primera hora. Estas subidas sitúan al índice en una posición potencialmente más sólida de cara a la decisión sobre las tasas de interés del Banco Central Europeo el jueves, en la que se espera que los responsables de la política monetaria mantengan estables los costos de financiación. "Esperamos que la presidenta del BCE, Christine Lagarde, transmita un mensaje equilibrado entre los riesgos al alza que siguen existiendo por los precios de la energía, los datos benignos de la inflación subyacente y unas condiciones financieras más restrictivas", escribieron analistas de Goldman Sachs. Los resultados de HSBC (HSBA.L) , el mayor banco de Europa, rompieron la reciente tendencia de buenos resultados en el sector bancario, lo que decepcionó a los inversores. Las acciones del banco con sede en Londres cayeron más de un 5%, tocando su mínimo en más de cuatro meses después de que sus ingresos no alcanzaran las previsiones, en parte debido a un crecimiento más lento en su negocio de gestión patrimonial. Estas caídas arrastraron al índice británico FTSE 100 (.FTSE) a un descenso del 0,75%. La bolsa francesa (.FCHI) subió un 0,51% tras caer más de un 2% la semana pasada, cuando las protestas sacudieron la segunda economía más grande de la zona del euro. La confianza de los consumidores franceses cayó en octubre hasta su nivel más bajo desde junio de 2013, según datos publicados el martes. Entre otras empresas destacadas, Novartis (NOVN.S) elevó sus previsiones de beneficio operativo básico para todo el año, lo que impulsó las acciones de la farmacéutica suiza un 1% al alza.

item.title: Four investors in talks to buy key parts of ammunition firm Forges de Tarbes, says minister
item.description: The French government is in talks with four, un-named investors to take over the key, technical know-how assets of Les Forges de Tarbes, French defence minister Catherine Vautrin said on Tuesday during a parliamentary committee.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The French government is in talks with four, un-named investors to take over the key, technical know-how assets of Les Forges de Tarbes, French defence minister Catherine Vautrin said on Tuesday during a parliamentary committee. Shell maker Forge de Tarbes, which supplies Franco-German tank maker KNDS for its Caesar howitzer, was placed under receivership this week. France has supplied Caesar howitzers to Ukraine after the Russian invasion of 2022.

item.title: NYSE moves to bring all-or-nothing options to stocks and company earnings
item.description: The New York Stock Exchange is preparing to start trading a new type of options contract that lets investors make all-or-nothing bets on whether a stock or exchange-traded fund will close above or below a set price.
item.dc:creator: Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: The New York Stock Exchange is preparing to start trading a new type of options contract that lets investors make all-or-nothing bets on whether a stock or exchange-traded fund will close above or below a set price. The launch comes as trading in options and event-based contracts has surged, prompting exchanges to develop new products that appeal to both retail and institutional investors looking for more precise ways to express market views and manage risk. NYSE is also seeking approval for a second product tied to company earnings metrics, the latest push by exchanges to capitalize on booming demand for event-driven trading. The binary return options contracts are expected to begin trading within days. The lineup includes 12 underlying securities, including Apple (AAPL.O) , Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Tesla (TSLA.O) and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust , with additional securities to be added over time. "We've seen this incredible growth in the US options market over the last several years. When we look inside that volume growth, there's a lot of interest in newer ways to trade or newer products to trade," said Kevin Tyrrell, chief product officer at NYSE. Options contracts give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell the underlying asset at a predetermined price. NYSE is also awaiting US Securities and Exchange Commission approval for binary key performance indicator, or KPI, options, which would pay investors based on whether a company reports a specified result above or below a certain threshold. Unlike traditional stock options, whose value is tied to share price moves, KPI options would allow investors to trade directly on metrics such as net sales, earnings per share, cloud-computing revenue or vehicle production. The cash-settled, European-style contracts, meaning they can be exercised only at expiration, would pay either $1 or nothing at expiration, depending on whether the reported metric meets the contract's strike level. Cboe Global Markets recently received approval for similar KPI-based contracts in partnership with Robinhood (HOOD.O) .

item.title: EssilorLuxottica has clear succession planning for top roles, director says
item.description: EssilorLuxottica has clear and strong succession plans for the role of chief executive and other senior executives, the head of the board's nominations committee at the French-Italian eyewear giant said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: EssilorLuxottica (ESLX.PA) has clear and strong succession plans for the role of chief executive and other senior executives, the head of the board's nominations committee at the French-Italian eyewear giant said on Tuesday. His comments follow a radio interview by one of the heirs of late Luxottica founder Leonardo Del Vecchio, who complained about EssilorLuxottica CEO Francesco Milleri's alleged failure to prepare for his eventual succession at the helm. "Any reports casting doubt on the strength of the succession planning at the top are entirely unfounded and damaging to the company's image and to the professionalism of its managers," Andrea Zappia, who chairs EssilorLuxottica's nominations and compensation committee, said in a statement. "There is a clear, well-defined and constantly updated succession plan for the roles of CEO and Deputy CEO and for all top positions, which, in line with the founder's vision, favors internal growth paths and has already proven its strength," Zappia added. He added the management team supporting Milleri - who was Del Vecchio's closest aide and chairs Delfin, the holding company that holds the family's EssilorLuxottica stake and other investments - had recently been reinforced and included "high-quality managers who can continue to grow". On Tuesday, Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio said his late father had tasked Milleri with leading the succession at the helm of the family's business empire, adding the EssilorLuxottica CEO had failed to fulfill such a mandate. Milleri comes up for renewal as CEO of EssilorLuxottica at the next general meeting, which is expected to be held in the spring.

item.title: Constellation gets conditional $5 billion US DOE loan commitment for nuclear plant upgrades
item.description: Constellation Energy said on Tuesday it received a conditional loan commitment of up to $5 billion from the US Department of Energy to fund nuclear uprates that will help it generate 1.1 gigawatts more power.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Constellation Energy (CEG.O) said on Tuesday it received a conditional loan commitment of up to $5 billion from the US Department of Energy to fund nuclear uprates that will help it generate 1.1 gigawatts more power. Demand for power in the US is growing after decades due to AI data center expansion, electrification of transportation and cryptocurrency mining. President Donald Trump set a goal to quadruple US nuclear power capacity by 2050. The US Department of Energy has hundreds of billions of dollars in financing available from its loan programs, the bulk of which is expected to support nuclear plants, according to energy secretary Chris Wright. Nuclear uprates increase power generation from existing reactors. The potential financing will help Constellation fund uprates at eight facilities in Illinois, Maryland and Pennsylvania, adding enough electricity to power more than 930,000 homes. This can lower costs and strengthen grid reliability in those states and across the PJM Interconnection and the Midcontinent Independent System Operator regions, the company said. Constellation, whose shares ticked up 1.8%, said the DOE-backed financing could reduce borrowing costs and speed up projects without having to build new plants or lay down transmission lines. Maryland-based Constellation is the largest US nuclear power plant operator. It owns a major fleet of natural-gas-fired as well as geothermal energy plants following its acquisition of electricity producer Calpine Corp earlier this year.

item.title: Judge hears Justice Dept's suit claiming noncitizens on California voter rolls
item.description: A US judge heard arguments on Tuesday on the Justice Department's request to block California from counting any mail ballots for the November 3 midterm elections from more than 20,000 registered voters the Trump administration alleges are likely noncitizens.
item.dc:creator: Luc Cohen, Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: A US judge heard arguments on Tuesday on the Justice Department's request to block California from counting any mail ballots for the November 3 midterm elections from more than 20,000 registered voters the Trump administration alleges are likely noncitizens. The Justice Department's October 15 lawsuit marked an escalation in President Donald Trump 's effort to boost the federal government's role in elections ahead of the midterms, with his Republican Party locked in a tight battle to retain control of both houses of Congress. The lawsuit is a rare intervention by the Justice Department in the voting process weeks before an election. The US Constitution assigns the responsibility of administering elections to individual states, though the federal government has some oversight role. US District Judge David Carter is holding a court hearing in Los Angeles to consider the department's request for a temporary restraining order barring officials from [USN:L6N46117W TEXT:"counting any ballots"] from the individuals it flagged. California has said the state's safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust. It said the Justice Department's assertions relied on "suspect data" and that complying with its demands would risk disenfranchising eligible voters. California is the most populous US state and a Democratic stronghold. It has more seats in the House of Representatives — 52 — than any other state. Trump has made California a focal point of his sweeping immigration crackdown since returning to the White House, accusing it of undermining public safety through its "sanctuary state" policies that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement. Trump has repeatedly insisted that states are not doing enough to stop voting by noncitizens, which he says is widespread despite multiple studies and state audits showing it is rare. CALIFORNIA SAYS SAFEGUARDS ARE ROBUST The hearing comes after a federal appeals court on Monday [USN:L2N46C163 TEXT:"rejected"] an unusual emergency request by the Justice Department asking the appeals court to temporarily block California from counting the ballots before Carter had the chance to rule. The Justice Department did not indicate how many of the more than 20,000 people it flagged in California had actually submitted a mail ballot. Apart from California, the Trump administration has sought to intervene in elections in two states that are home to [USN:L6N4670ZS TEXT:"competitive races"]. In Alaska, the Justice Department last week asked a judge to [USN:L2N46D019 TEXT:"prevent certification"] of election results if the Republican incumbent senator loses by a slim margin, alleging that the presence of another candidate with a similar name on the ballot could confuse voters. Alaska has urged that the case be dismissed, arguing it has taken steps to distinguish the two candidates on the ballot. In Washington state, the Justice Department on Monday [USN:L6N46D0UP TEXT:"sent a letter"] asking officials not to count any ballots received from 400 voters it said may not be citizens. Washington's top elections official said the timing of the request indicated it was intended to cast unfounded suspicion on election results. California had 23 million registered voters as of December 2025, while Washington had 5 million registered voters as of 2024, state records show. Voting rights activists have expressed concern that the federal government's methods for scrutinizing state voter lists to identify noncitizen voters risk wrongly flagging naturalized citizens for removal from the rolls.

item.title: Trump says he will visit tanker in Texas with first oil from Venezuela deal
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he planned to visit a tanker in Texas which contains the first oil received from Venezuela following a deal that Washington made after deposing the country's former leader.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he planned to visit a tanker in Texas which contains the first oil received from Venezuela following a deal that Washington made after deposing the country's former leader. [USN:FWN44P1ZC TEXT:"Trump announced in August an agreement"] that grants the United States access to a fifth of Venezuela's crude reserves. "They've sent me as a gift a boatload of a million barrels of oil, and I'm giving that to the United States of America," Trump told reporters. He later said in a post on Truth Social that this was the "first shipment of BILLIONS of Barrels to come." The White House said in September that oil from the Venezuela deal would probably hit US reserves in November. The United States has been working closely with the interim government led by acting President Delcy Rodriguez since US forces captured President Nicolas Maduro in January.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro viaja para os EUA após derrota na eleição, dizem fontes
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro viajou para os Estados Unidos, disseram à Reuters um aliado próximo do parlamentar e uma fonte do governo dos EUA nesta terça-feira, menos de 24 horas após o senador assegurar que nunca pensou em deixar o país e depois da derrota eleitoral no domingo para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: Flávio Bolsonaro viajou para os Estados Unidos, disseram à Reuters um aliado próximo do parlamentar e uma fonte do governo dos EUA nesta terça-feira, menos de 24 horas após o senador assegurar que nunca pensou em deixar o país e depois da derrota eleitoral no domingo para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. A Embaixada dos EUA no Brasil não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. Não ficou imediatamente claro para qual local exatamente Flávio Bolsonaro estava indo, a que horas chegaria ou se pediria asilo nos EUA. O governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, já alegou que o pai de Flávio, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, foi vítima de perseguição judicial no Brasil. Flávio descumpriu uma decisão do ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), para que entregasse seus passaportes nesta terça-feira pela manhã, o que levou a Polícia Federal a cancelar os passaportes do senador, inclusive o diplomático. A Reuters não conseguiu confirmar com quem o senador viajou aos EUA, mas apurou com uma fonte que as duas filhas do parlamentar não foram para a escola em Brasília nesta terça. "Eu nunca pensei em sair do país. Eu vou entregar os meus passaportes e vou me defender dessa aberração, que é uma clara tentativa de me intimidar", disse Flávio em vídeo publicado em sua conta no Instagram na segunda-feira, afirmando ainda que organizaria a oposição ao governo Lula. Moraes determinou a entrega dos passaportes de Flávio no âmbito de um inquérito em que o senador é investigado por lavagem de dinheiro juntamente com o advogado Willer Tomaz, amigo do senador. Ambos os acusados negam qualquer irregularidade. A decisão do ministro do STF foi tomada após o ex-deputado Eduardo Bolsonaro, irmão de Flávio, dizer em uma transmissão nas redes sociais que Flávio deveria deixar o país caso perdesse a eleição presidencial. A viagem de Flávio para os Estados Unidos repetiria os passos do pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, que viajou para os Estados Unidos depois de se recusar a reconhecer a derrota para Lula na eleição presidencial de 2022. Jair Bolsonaro acabou retornando ao Brasil, mas posteriormente foi condenado a 27 anos de prisão por tentativa de golpe de Estado. Flávio ainda não reconheceu oficialmente a derrota no domingo. No dia da votação, afirmou que buscaria a anulação do resultado alegando irregularidades após a prorrogação do prazo de votação. Posteriormente, disse que pediria a cassação da chapa de Lula ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE). No entanto, seu partido, o PL, declarou na segunda-feira que reconhecia a vitória de Lula.

item.title: US agency is again probing if Polymarket broke 2022 settlement, sources says
item.description: A US regulator is investigating whether prediction market operator Polymarket violated a 2022 enforcement deal in which it promised to ban US users from its main overseas platform, reviving an inquiry the agency shuttered last year without bringing charges, said two people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Chris Prentice
item.content:encoded: A US regulator is investigating whether prediction market operator Polymarket violated a 2022 enforcement deal in which it promised to ban US users from its main overseas platform, [USN:L1N3ML0V9 TEXT:"reviving an inquiry"] the agency shuttered last year without bringing charges, said two people familiar with the matter. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is probing whether Polymarket took sufficient steps to keep US users off the platform as part of a broader investigation it opened into the company earlier this year, the people said. One of the people said the scrutiny is focused on Polymarket's past controls and processes. The agency is examining Polymarket's controls for determining where customers are located, as well as its advertising activities in the United States, as part of that inquiry, the people said. Polymarket is based in New York and has an offshore entity registered in Panama. The CFTC is also scrutinizing Polymarket's US platform, which the company began rolling out late last year, including its customer onboarding processes and customer protections, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss confidential enforcement issues. Reuters is reporting these elements of the probe for the first time. The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg News and other media first reported in June that the CFTC was broadly probing Polymarket, but provided few details. Bloomberg added that the CFTC was looking into social media activity tied to the company. Spokespeople for the CFTC and Polymarket declined to comment. Probes are not necessarily an indication of wrongdoing and many do not result in enforcement action. The new details, nevertheless, raise fresh questions over why the CFTC and Justice Department last year closed similar probes into whether Polymarket had violated the 2022 settlement, which resolved CFTC allegations at the time that Polymarket had been operating in the US unlawfully since its launch in 2020. Neither agency has commented on the decision to close the probes and a Justice Department spokesperson declined to comment for this story. Prediction markets allow traders to bet on real-world events, including sports, government policy announcements and [USN:L4N45Y17K TEXT:"elections"]. Aided by supportive policies under President Donald Trump's second administration, the industry has surged over the past two years. Trump's son, Donald Trump Jr, is a Polymarket investor. As the platforms have grown, they have drawn scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers and advocacy groups worried the platforms are creating new avenues for [USN:L6N41C1D6 TEXT:"insider trading"], while recent political upsets, [USN:L6N46C031 TEXT:"including in Brazil"] this week, have raised questions about their accuracy. Polymarket has said it has revamped controls. The firm says it expressly prohibits the use of virtual private networks (VPNs) or similar tools to circumvent its geographic restrictions, and has extensive controls to monitor for misconduct and to prevent restricted users from accessing its offshore platform. [USN:L6N44P0U4 TEXT:"Speaking to Reuters in August"], Shana Bautista, Polymarket's global head of investigations and intelligence, said US users circumventing its restrictions was not "a really prevalent issue." BIDEN ADMINISTRATION AGENCIES OPENED PROBE IN 2024 Under the 2022 settlement negotiated by the CFTC's former Biden-era leadership, Polymarket agreed to stop offering its market to US users. But as 2024 US election bets on the platform grew, political pundits and social media users [USN:L1N3LU0ST TEXT:"questioned whether Americans"] were circumventing Polymarket's restrictions. Months before the election, the CFTC opened a probe into whether Polymarket was complying with the deal, [USN:L1N3ML0V9 TEXT:"Reuters"] and other media reported at the time. The Justice Department opened a related investigation, with the [USN:L1N3MK1FR TEXT:"FBI searching"] Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan's New York home in November 2024. Two months later, the Trump administration took office and appointed new leaders to both agencies. On July 15, 2025, Coplan said in an X post that the CFTC and Justice Department had closed their probes and cleared the company of any wrongdoing. A week later, Polymarket said it had bought a CFTC-licensed derivatives exchange, which became the platform for its US operation. CFTC-registered platforms must comply with certain customer protection and market abuse prevention requirements. While CFTC data shows the agency's overall enforcement activity has slumped during Trump's second presidency, its enforcement director David Miller [USN:SPN40F00M TEXT:"said during his first month on the job in March"] that he would aggressively police prediction markets. In April, [USN:FWN41616V TEXT:"the agency and Justice Department charged"] a US soldier, alleging he made $400,000 from insider bets on Polymarket's offshore platform, sparking fresh questions about its controls. According to the indictment, Gannon Ken Van Dyke, who has pleaded not guilty, accessed the platform using a VPN and "exit mode," which geolocated to a foreign country. Polymarket said at the time that it had referred the matter to the authorities.

item.title: 49ers' Kittle says sour taste from first loss will fuel team
item.description: San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle said the team will carry the sting of their first loss of the season into their bye week, a mood he believes could help sharpen a battered roster that have built their identity around physical football.
item.dc:creator: Rory Carroll
item.content:encoded: San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle said the team will carry the sting of their first loss of the season into their bye week, a mood he believes could help sharpen a battered roster that have built their identity around physical football. The 49ers returned from Atlanta disappointed with their 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday but encouraged by the prospect of getting several injured players back after the break, Kittle told Reuters in a Zoom interview on Monday. "Losing is not fun," Kittle said. "But it is really hard to win in football. Everybody's a professional, everybody's talented." But he said the defeat could give San Francisco a needed edge during the now 6-1 team's time away from the field. "Instead of, 'Hey, we're going on this bye week, we're just going to go enjoy ourselves, forget about everything,' you're kind of sitting there angry for the entire week," Kittle said. "And I think that'll be good for our football team." MOUNTING INJURIES The loss came as San Francisco have been hit hard by injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Kittle said the team had effectively lost all of their training-camp receivers, an unusual strain on an offense that has relied heavily on its remaining playmakers. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel were among those who were unavailable on Sunday but expected to return in Week Nine. Still, the veteran tight end said the 49ers' depth — especially contributions from recent draft classes — has bolstered his confidence that the team can contend for a championship. "We have young players who are out there making plays," Kittle said, pointing to rookies and younger players rotating along the defensive line and contributing elsewhere on defense. "We don't have to win every game on the shoulders of Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey, or Nick Bosa and Fred Warner." VIOLENT GAME The injuries, Kittle said, are partly an unavoidable consequence of how San Francisco play. "We pride ourselves on playing a very violent game of football," he said. "When you turn on our tape, our whole offense, we're running off the ball, we're hitting people, we are blocking. Our defense is flying around, hitting people as hard as they possibly can." That approach creates wear and tear over a long season, he said, but it is not something the 49ers intend to change. "We sit on violence, and that's the way that we think football should be played," Kittle said. "I wouldn't change how we play because that's what makes us us." Kittle pointed to the 2021 season as an example of a San Francisco team overcoming early injuries. The 49ers started that year 2-4 before winning eight straight games to reach the playoffs and advancing to the NFC Championship Game. INJURY COMEBACK This season has also presented a personal challenge for Kittle, who said he spent most of the close season recovering from an Achilles injury. Rather than his usual summer regimen of route-running and blocking work, he said his rehabilitation consisted largely of calf raises for months. Kittle said he did not return to practice until shortly before the team's trip to Australia to open the season, leaving him little time to regain football conditioning before playing again. "I definitely felt a lot of rust early on," he said. "But the more that I play, the more that I practice, the more I'm starting to feel like myself again." He said he has felt closer to full football condition over the past two weeks. "When something like that's taken away from you, it hurts," Kittle said. "But it also lights a fire in you every single day." CANCER SCREENINGS Away from the field, Kittle is working with Novartis on a prostate-cancer awareness campaign built around blood-test screening. Kittle said the partnership resonated because his grandfather had prostate cancer and survived it before later dying. He said he was struck by learning that one in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer and that early detection can substantially improve outcomes. "The point is to make it comfortable," Kittle said, adding that many men are reluctant to discuss screening. "You literally just go get a blood test. It's so much easier and it's not daunting." For now, though, Kittle said the 49ers will take an unhappy break and use it as motivation for the stretch ahead. "I'll be pretty grumpy," he said. "I know I'm a positive guy, but I get grumpy too sometimes."

item.title: GM to offer hybrid SUVs in strategic pivot from electric
item.description: General Motors plans to introduce hybrid versions of its popular three-row SUVs, people familiar with the matter said, in a strategic shift after heavily investing in electric vehicles.
item.dc:creator: Kalea Hall, David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: General Motors (GM.N) plans to introduce hybrid versions of its popular three-row SUVs, people familiar with the matter said, in a strategic shift after heavily investing in electric vehicles. The US automaker plans to build hybrid models of the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave and GMC Acadia at a factory in Lansing, Michigan, the people told Reuters. The mechanically similar models are among GM's strongest sellers in the US. GM said in a statement after Reuters reported the plans on Tuesday that it plans to invest in its Lansing Delta Township assembly plant to prepare for hybrid-vehicle production. It did not provide details on timing or models. GM CEO SAYS HYBRIDS ARE COMING CEO Mary Barra told analysts during GM's earnings call last week that the carmaker would have hybrids in multiple segments. "It's not going to be additional (capital expenditures) and engineering," she said, adding that GM would say more about them as it got closer to launch. US [USN:L6N41K18Q TEXT:"hybrid sales have taken off"] as car shoppers seek relief from higher gas prices. GM, which only sells a hybrid version of the Chevy Corvette in the US, has lost market share this year, while strong hybrid players like Toyota have gained. Dealers have complained about [USN:L6N4570VU TEXT:"GM's lack of hybrids"], which combine a gas engine with a lithium-ion battery and electric motor to conserve fuel and boost power. GM DEALERS SAY THEY WANT HYBRIDS Dealers have been pressing the company to add hybrids to its lineup, some of those who have attended recent regional meetings between retailers and GM sales executives told Reuters. "We've been telling them every chance we get that we need hybrids," one dealer said. GM executives have in the past said hybrids add too much cost and complexity, and that they preferred to invest in EVs. Hybrids also didn't help GM meet stringent emissions standards that Trump's administration has upended. GM's US market share dropped to 16.6% in the first nine months of the year, from 17.4% a year before, while hybrid leaders Toyota and Honda gained. GM's hybrid plans have emerged days before the November 3 midterm congressional election, where several key Michigan seats are up for grabs. US President Donald Trump's administration has been eager to advertise its efforts to support US auto manufacturing. Energy Department Assistant Secretary Audrey Robertson is scheduled to tour the Lansing factory where GM plans to make the hybrids later on Tuesday. The department is restructuring a previously awarded grant to GM to support EV production at a nearby Lansing plant to now support hybrid production. In 2024, under President Joe Biden, the Energy Department awarded GM $500 million to retool another nearby Michigan assembly plant to build EVs but the money was not released. GM said those funds will go to its Lansing Delta Township for future hybrid production. The department did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: JetBlue CEO says no creditor talks as bond selloff raises doubts about turnaround
item.description: JetBlue Airways is not in talks with its creditors and is not considering a debt restructuring, CEO Joanna Geraghty told Reuters on Tuesday, as the airline seeks to calm concerns about its financial health following a sharp selloff in its bonds. Her comments came days after a group of creditors hired restructuring advisers PJT Partners and Akin Gump, according to media reports, raising questions about the carrier's ability to manage its debt.
item.dc:creator: Doyinsola Oladipo
item.content:encoded: JetBlue Airways (JBLU.O) is not in talks with its creditors and is not considering a debt restructuring, CEO Joanna Geraghty told Reuters on Tuesday, as the airline seeks to calm concerns about its financial health following a sharp selloff in its bonds. Her comments came days after a group of creditors hired restructuring advisers PJT Partners and Akin Gump, according to media reports, raising questions about the carrier's ability to manage its debt. The concern among investors is whether JetBlue can fund its turnaround without having to renegotiate its debt. The airline has about $8.4 billion in debt and finance lease obligations, has not posted an annual profit since 2019 and saw its nine-month net loss nearly double to $823 million amid soaring fuel costs. "We are not in talks with our creditors," Geraghty said. "Part of today, as I mentioned, was to really set the record straight that we're making progress in the underlying business." When asked if the airline was pursuing any financial support from the US government, Geraghty said it was not. She also reiterated that debt restructuring was not under consideration. Separately, Geraghty met with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick last week to discuss a range of issues, according to a person briefed on the matter. JetBlue declined to comment on whether the meeting occurred. The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The company's roughly $2 billion in bonds backed by its TrueBlue frequent-flyer program were trading at about $47 for every $100 of debt on October 26, down from around $80 at the start of the month, according to LSEG data. The steep drop pushed yields, the returns investors demand for holding the bonds, above 30%, signaling growing concerns about the airline's ability to repay its debt. "Our results tell a very different story from what our bondholders are communicating out there in the market," she said in an interview. FUNDING THE TURNAROUND JetBlue used $273 million in cash from operations in the first nine months of 2026, nearly double the $143 million a year earlier. Its unrestricted cash and investments fell about $850 million since December to $1.6 billion at September-end, partly reflecting aircraft purchases. The airline faces scheduled debt and finance lease repayments of $477 million in 2027 and $582 million in 2028, before a larger $1.8 billion comes due in 2029, according to its quarterly filing. JetBlue reported $2.2 billion in liquidity and about $7 billion in assets not already pledged to lenders that could help it raise additional funds. In its quarterly filing, JetBlue said it had enough liquidity to meet its needs for at least the next 12 months. Executives also expressed confidence on Tuesday that the airline could secure additional financing to support its turnaround through 2028. The company expects another $250 million in aircraft-backed financing in the fourth quarter. On Tuesday's earnings call, Geraghty also identified potential funding sources beyond traditional borrowing, including JetBlue's Paisly travel business, venture investments and co-branded credit-card partnership, but gave no details of any specific plans. Despite stronger ticket revenue, soaring fuel costs continue to undermine its recovery. Third-quarter revenue rose 21%, but fuel expenses jumped 61%. JetBlue now expects a full-year adjusted operating margin of negative 4.5% to negative 6.5%, worse than the negative 2% to negative 5% forecast in July. The airline still aims to return to operating profitability in 2027 and generate positive free cash flow in 2028.

item.title: Seahawks acquire All-Pro G Quenton Nelson from Colts
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks acquired eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Seattle Seahawks acquired eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts on Tuesday. The Colts received a third-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and a fifth-round selection in 2028 in the deal, which is pending a physical exam. Nelson, 30, is playing in the final season of a four-year, $80 million contract. The trade allows the Colts to receive some compensation, as opposed to letting him walk at the end of the season. A first-team All-Pro in each of his first three seasons, Nelson has started all seven games in 2026 and all 136 in which he has played since being selected by the Colts with the sixth overall pick of the 2018 NFL Draft out of Notre Dame. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pope's cancer is a 'gamechanger' for papacy, Vatican foreign minister says
item.description: Pope Leo's lung cancer diagnosis and surgery has affected how Catholics view his health and papacy, the Vatican's foreign minister said on Tuesday, an unusually frank assessment by one of the Church's most senior officials.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: Pope Leo 's lung cancer diagnosis and surgery has affected how Catholics view his health and papacy, the Vatican's foreign minister said on Tuesday, an unusually frank assessment by one of the Church's most senior officials. "It's a bit of a gamechanger," Archbishop Paul Gallagher told journalists at an event in Rome. Leo, 71, had part of one lung removed in surgery earlier this month. His doctors have said the cancer was localized and had not spread, and the pope [USN:L1N46710S TEXT:"will not require"] further treatment. Gallagher said that given Leo's relatively young age for a pope and his physical fitness, some Catholics had thought he was a "Superman" pope. The illness revealed that Leo "is a poor mortal like the rest of us," said the archbishop. "I think that is going to change how we see him and possibly how he sees himself as well," said Gallagher, a Briton who has served in his Vatican role since 2014. POPE EXCITED ABOUT LATIN AMERICA TRIP Leo was diagnosed with [USN:L8N46006S TEXT:"lung adenocarcinoma"], the most common form of lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung in an operation on October 13. The pope has been gradually resuming his schedule since returning to the Vatican on October 18 and has appeared energetic at public events, speaking in a firm, clear voice. The Vatican confirmed on Monday he would go forward with a three-country, November 6-17 visit across South America, one of the most intense foreign tours arranged for a pope [USN:L8N45D0VL TEXT:"in decades"]. "All of the medical advice is very positive ... so he feels he can go," Gallagher said in response to a question about why the pope is travelling [USN:L5N46D0QL TEXT:"only 24 days after his surgery"]. "I think he's going on this trip very simply because he wants to go on it," said the archbishop. "It was obviously quite advanced in the planning." UKRAINE CEASEFIRE, PAPAL VISIT TO US Separately, Gallagher also addressed the recent [USN:L1N46911P TEXT:"ceasefire"] agreed by Russia and Ukraine to allow aid into the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky. He said that while Leo had recently spoken with both Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, he did not believe the Vatican was involved in arranging the ceasefire. "I don't think we were," said Gallagher. He also spoke about the Vatican's ongoing agreement with China on the appointment of Catholic bishops in the communist state, and acknowledged "imperfections" with the accord. The deal, first signed in 2018, gives Chinese officials some input into whom Leo appoints as bishops in the country. "It's not easy, the dialogue is not easy. The imperfections of the agreement are evident, but there is a commitment to persevere in dialogue ... and that is what will continue to happen," said Gallagher. The archbishop also said he expects Leo, the first US-born pope, to visit the United States "in the not too distant future." But he said the visit might not occur in 2027, depending on the pope's commitments.

item.title: Higher tariffs on Canadian imports would be 'catastrophic,' Honda exec says
item.description: A pending increase in US tariffs on steel and auto imports from Canada starting January 1 would be “catastrophic” for the industry, Honda Motor’s head of public affairs said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson, Kalea Hall
item.content:encoded: A pending increase in US tariffs on steel and auto imports from Canada starting January 1 would be “catastrophic” for the industry, Honda Motor’s (7267.T) head of public affairs said on Tuesday. Automakers are closely watching talks between the US, Mexico and Canada, hoping the countries extend a longstanding trade deal. The three countries' auto industries are tightly intertwined, and higher tariffs could raise costs and affect where companies such as Honda build new plants. "We need that trilateral agreement to stay in place in order for the US industry to be competitive. It's integral to our success," said Jennifer Thomas, senior vice president of corporate affairs for American Honda Motor Co, speaking at the Reuters Automotive USA conference in Detroit. The auto industry has been grappling with tariffs since early 2025, when President Donald Trump’s administration placed varying tariff rates on imports from multiple countries, including Mexico and Canada. “I am cautiously optimistic that cooler heads will prevail, and we will avoid that January 1 doubling of the tariffs, because that really would be catastrophic just for the entire industry,” Thomas said. The US and Canada are [USN:L2N46C11U TEXT:"working on a deal"] to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, Reuters reported on Monday. Those talks are aimed at tariffs imposed under Section 232 of US trade law, including a tariff of up to 50% on Canadian steel and a 25% tariff on autos, with negotiators discussing potential relief from those duties. Unlike trade deals with the EU, Japan or South Korea, the trade pact between Mexico, Canada and the US has specific North American content requirements known as "rules of origin." In the negotiations with Mexico, the US has demanded that all North American-built vehicles contain 50% US-specific content, a figure that would drive regional required content up to 82% to qualify for US benefits, sources familiar with the talks have said. Vehicles assembled in Mexico and Canada would likely still be charged some level of tariffs, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer has said. Thomas and other auto executives said that rules-of-origin requirements are not in place in other trade deals. “Right now, North America is at an unfair disadvantage,” Thomas said. In August, Honda said it may not build an eighth assembly plant in North America unless the trade deal between the three countries is extended. “We are at capacity, and so we're exploring all options. And at the end of the day, we're going to continue to invest in the US,” Thomas said.

item.title: Robinhood CEO's AI startup Harmonic expands into software, chip design verification

item.content:encoded: Harmonic, the AI startup co-founded by Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev, said on Tuesday it was expanding its Aristotle model from mathematical proofs into software and chip design verification, as AI's growing use in detecting software flaws draws increased scrutiny. Researchers recently used the technology to uncover critical bugs in PHP, prompting a global rush to patch the vulnerabilities. Here are more details: Backed by Nvidia's venture capital arm, NVentures, Sequoia and Ribbit Capital, Harmonic raised $120 million in a funding round last November that valued it at $1.45 billion Harmonic is developing what it calls "mathematical superintelligence," a reasoning-focused AI system aimed at reducing hallucinations and factual errors The company said Aristotle can now verify software written in C and chip designs written in Verilog US fusion lab DIII-D said Aristotle rebuilt part of its reactor-control software in four hours from one research paper and a 254-word prompt Aristotle is available with usage-based pricing

item.title: Trump to roll back methane rules in latest Texas campaign push
item.description: President Donald Trump will use a campaign swing through Texas on Tuesday to announce a plan to ease methane rules for oil and gas producers, seeking to show voters he is working to bring down gasoline prices a week before the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Steve Holland, Jarrett Renshaw
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump will use a campaign swing through Texas on Tuesday to announce a plan to ease methane rules for oil and gas producers, seeking to show voters he is working to bring down gasoline prices a week before the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]. The move is the latest in a [USN:L1N4670FM TEXT:"string of pre-election steps"] by Trump to address fuel prices, which have become a political liability for Republicans amid the war with Iran. By pairing the methane rollback with rallies for his hand-picked Senate candidate Ken Paxton, Trump is trying to turn energy policy into votes in a longtime Republican stronghold. The trip marks Trump's third visit to Texas this month to mobilize support for Paxton, with rallies planned in Corpus Christi and Lubbock. Paxton is locked in a close race with Democrat James Talarico, and a loss next Tuesday would complicate the Republican Party's path to retaining its slim Senate majority. Trump plans to announce an Environmental Protection Agency proposal to roll back Biden-era rules that required companies to fix leaky equipment and regularly check wells for escaping methane, a potent greenhouse gas, a White House official said. The administration is casting it as a way to produce more energy and lower costs. The plan would give relief to small, low-output wells and end a program that used outside groups to report large methane leaks, the official said. It would also ease rules aimed at phasing out the routine burning off of gas at oil wells. Trump's repeated trips to Texas are part of a broader push in Republican-leaning states, which were expected to be safely in hand but have instead become midterm battlegrounds. His October campaign blitz has also taken him to Oklahoma, Alabama, Nebraska, Iowa, Ohio, South Carolina and Mississippi. Trump has publicly criticized his longtime ally, calling Paxton "a pain in the ass sometimes," while making it clear he prefers him to Talarico. Tech billionaire Elon Musk and other donors are [USN:L6N4660XW TEXT:"pouring hundreds of millions"] into a late effort to rescue Paxton's campaign.

item.title: West Virginia law shielding addresses of judges, officers is unconstitutional, court rules
item.description: A federal appeals court ruled on Tuesday that a West Virginia law barring the online publication of home addresses and unpublished phone numbers belonging to judges and law enforcement officers is unconstitutional.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A federal appeals court ruled on Tuesday that a West Virginia law barring the online publication of home addresses and unpublished phone numbers belonging to judges and law enforcement officers is unconstitutional. The ruling by the 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals marked the first time a federal appellate court has struck down one of the many laws states enacted safeguarding such information after a disgruntled lawyer [USN:KCN24Z20N TEXT:"shot and killed"] the son of US District Judge Esther Salas at her home in New Jersey in 2020. The ruling came in class-action lawsuits filed by retired law enforcement officer Michael Jackson against Thomson Reuters (TRI.TO) , Whitepages Inc, Thryv (THRY.O) , PeopleConnect and RELX's (REL.L) LexisNexis alleging they violated West Virginia's Daniel’s Law by publishing home addresses and unpublished phone numbers of individuals covered by the law through their online people-search services. Samir Deger-Sen, a lawyer at Latham & Watkins who represented PeopleConnect and argued the appeal on behalf of all the defendants, in a statement welcomed the ruling, saying the court had affirmed that addresses and phone numbers "warrant robust protection under the First Amendment." "We hope the decision will encourage thoughtful deliberation among state legislatures evaluating similar legislation, particularly as they consider whether there are less restrictive means to accomplish their goals," he said. A spokesperson for Thomson Reuters, the parent company of Reuters, in a statement said it "has long been committed to honoring privacy and keeping personal data safe" and believed West Virginia's law "attempts to serve a laudable goal." "But in its current form, the statute is overbroad and violates the First Amendment," the spokesperson said. Jackson's lawyer, Philip Fraietta of Bursor & Fisher, did not respond to a request for comment. West Virginia enacted the law in 2021 after the fatal shooting of Salas' 20-year-old son, Daniel Anderl, by a lawyer who went to the judge's residence after finding her home address online. Her husband was also wounded. More than a dozen states have [USN:L1N4161D1 TEXT:"adopted their own versions"] of Daniel's Law, including Salas' home state of New Jersey, whose own measure [USN:L6N44912Z TEXT:"remains subject to litigation"]. Congress [USN:L1N3361D8 TEXT:"also passed"] the Daniel Anderl Judicial Security and Privacy Act in 2022 to similarly protect federal judges' personal information online. West Virginia's law prohibited disclosure of covered officials' home addresses or unpublished telephone numbers without their permission and allowed lawsuits seeking at least $1,000 per violation, punitive damages, attorney fees and injunctive relief. US District Judge Michael Urbanski dismissed Jackson’s lawsuits last year after concluding the law violated the US Constitution's First and Fourteenth Amendments, which protect speech and due process rights. The 4th Circuit agreed in Tuesday's three-judge opinion, saying the law imposed a content-based restriction on speech that was not narrowly tailored to serve the state's interest of ensuring the safety of judges and law enforcement officials. "West Virginia was fully justified in attempting to regulate such speech in light of the compelling government interest in enhancing the safety and security of certain public officials, but its efforts reached more broadly (than) necessary to accomplish the task," US Circuit Judge Paul Niemeyer wrote for the panel. He highlighted a key distinction between West Virginia’s statute and similar laws elsewhere: It did not require officials to notify a company that information was improperly posted and request its removal before suing. As a result, Niemeyer said, data brokers could face liability for publishing information on a broad group of people that, unbeknownst to the companies, included protected officials’ information. The law therefore forced companies to choose between potential liability and self-censorship, discouraging the publication of otherwise lawful information, he wrote. "As a result, data brokers either face liability or they self-censor and do not publish such information," Neimeyer wrote. The case is Jackson v Thomson Reuters, 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals, No. 25-2121. For the plaintiff: Philip Fraietta of Bursor & Fisher For the defense: Samir of Latham & Watkins Read more: [USN:L6N44912Z TEXT:"New Jersey ruling could imperil state law aimed at protecting judges' personal data"] [USN:L1N4161D1 TEXT:"NJ judge whose son was killed warns against weakening state data privacy laws"] [USN:L1N3LN0UC TEXT:"Litigation funder backs cases over NJ law shielding info on judges, officials"] [USN:L1N3JT15A TEXT:"New Jersey defends privacy law shielding judges, prosecutors"]

item.title: Prediction market Kalshi expands safeguards for young traders
item.description: Kalshi is strengthening guardrail for young-adult traders on its prediction market platform, as it seeks to curb addiction and promote responsible trading ahead of US midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kalshi is strengthening guardrail for young-adult traders on its prediction market platform, as it seeks to curb addiction and promote responsible trading ahead of US midterm elections. The safeguards will be applicable for traders aged between 18 and 20 years, Kalshi said on Tuesday The category of traders will start with a $2,500 monthly deposit limit, creating a prevention to massive losses that can be incurred on the platform Kalshi will alert new traders with balances exceeding $1,000 who allocate more than 25% of their funds to a single trade, encouraging them to diversify While prediction market platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket have gained popularity by enabling users to wager on outcomes ranging from sports and elections to military operations, they have drawn criticism from those who argue the platforms resemble gambling and carry addiction risk "Like the stock exchange, Kalshi is available only to traders 18 and older," Luana Lopes Lara, chief operating officer and co-founder of Kalshi, said, adding that new traders need more education and safeguards The company also announced new partnerships with parent and youth safety organizations — Parent ProTech and ConnectSafely — to publish parent's guides to prediction markets

item.title: US court of appeals affirms validity of Venezuela's PDVSA 2020 bonds
item.description: A US court of appeals on Tuesday affirmed the validity of bonds issued by Venezuela's state-run oil firm PDVSA maturing in 2020, which were defaulted, saying pre-approval from the South American country's National Assembly was not required.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A US court of appeals on Tuesday affirmed the validity of bonds issued by Venezuela's state-run oil firm PDVSA maturing in 2020, which were defaulted, saying pre-approval from the South American country's National Assembly was not required. The decision by the US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, which discussed the case this year, reaffirmed a judgment by the US District Court for the Southern District of New York, which concluded that the Venezuelan Constitution did not invalidate the bonds' offer. The bonds are particularly important since they were collateralized with equity in one of the parent companies of Venezuela-owned US refiner Citgo Petroleum. Bondholders have been seeking compensation since the default. The bond traded flat on Tuesday at 114.25 cents on the dollar.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro headed to the US after losing Brazil election, sources say
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election and refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to hand over his passports, two sources said.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito, Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election and refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to hand over his passports, two sources said. The US Embassy in Brazil did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Bolsonaro's lawyer also did not respond. It was not immediately clear where Bolsonaro was heading, what time he would arrive or whether he would seek asylum. US President Donald Trump's administration has previously alleged Flavio's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil. Flavio's departure for the United States threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas. Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to put them back in power, and Reuters reported ahead of Sunday's election on [USN:L1N4650X8 TEXT:"a US State Department"] campaign to restore them to office. Trump made no mention of Bolsonaro's departure in comments to the press on Monday, but said the Brazilian vote "looked like another rigged election." Lula's office did not respond to a request for comment. Bolsonaro was favored to win Sunday's presidential election but ended up [USN:L2N46B01X TEXT:"losing"] in a shock result to Lula. On Monday, he was given 24 hours to surrender his passports as part of a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing, but his documents were cancelled after the deadline lapsed, two other sources said. Bolsonaro, who loses his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, said on Monday he had no plans to flee. "I have never thought about leaving the country," he said. "I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me." Brazil's Minister of Institutional Relations Jose Guimaraes commented on reports of Bolsonaro leaving the country in an interview with CNN Brasil. "I have no confirmation from the Federal Police or oversight bodies," he told the news outlet. "But this speaks a lot about our opponent’s lack of preparation to govern the country." FOLLOWING FATHER'S PATH Jair Bolsonaro also went to the United States after refusing to concede to Lula in 2022, when former US President Joe Biden was in office. He eventually returned to Brazil but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia. His son has yet to officially concede defeat — saying on Sunday he would seek the annulment of the result over alleged voter irregularities — but his Liberal Party said on Monday it acknowledged Lula's victory. It remains unclear how Bolsonaro was able to leave the country while he was facing a 24-hour deadline to hand over his passports. A senior Federal Police official said Bolsonaro had not exited the country via any regular migration point. Eduardo Bolsonaro, Bolsonaro's younger brother who lives in the United States, said ahead of the vote that an election loss would require a move. "If my brother does not win, I'm in favor that he would leave the country," he told podcaster Steven Crowder this month.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro se dirige a EEUU tras su derrota electoral en Brasil: fuentes
item.description: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro abandonó el país con destino a Estados Unidos tras haber perdido las elecciones presidenciales del domingo y negarse a cumplir la orden del Supremo Tribunal Federal de entregar su pasaporte, informaron dos fuentes.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito, Luciana Novaes Magalhaes
item.content:encoded: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro abandonó el país con destino a Estados Unidos tras haber perdido las elecciones presidenciales del domingo y negarse a cumplir la orden del Supremo Tribunal Federal de entregar su pasaporte, informaron dos fuentes. La embajada de Estados Unidos en Brasil no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. El abogado de Bolsonaro tampoco quiso hacer declaraciones. No estaba claro inmediatamente cuál era su destino, a qué hora llegaría o si tiene intención de solicitar asilo. La administración del presidente estadounidense Donald Trump había sostenido previamente que el padre de Flávio, el exmandatario Jair Bolsonaro, era víctima de persecución judicial en Brasil. La partida de Flávio Bolsonaro hacia Estados Unidos amenaza con profundizar la brecha entre las dos naciones más pobladas de América. El presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ha acusado a Washington de confabularse con los Bolsonaro para devolverlos al poder. Reuters informó antes de las elecciones del domingo sobre una campaña del Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos para restituirlos en sus cargos. Bolsonaro era el favorito para ganar las elecciones presidenciales del domingo, pero acabó perdiendo por sorpresa frente al izquierdista Lula. El lunes se le concedieron 24 horas para entregar su pasaporte como parte de una investigación por blanqueo de capitales, en la que él niega haber cometido algún delito, pero el plazo ya venció, según indicaron otras dos fuentes, lo que ha llevado a la anulación de sus documentos. No está claro si podría ingresar a Estados Unidos con sus pasaportes anulados. Jair Bolsonaro también se trasladó a Estados Unidos tras haberse negado a reconocer su derrota frente a Lula en 2022, durante el mandato del entonces presidente estadounidense Joe Biden. Posteriormente regresó a Brasil, pero fue condenado a 27 años de prisión por conspirar para dar un golpe de Estado, luego de que sus seguidores irrumpieran en edificios gubernamentales en Brasilia. Su hijo aún no ha reconocido oficialmente la derrota -el domingo anunció que solicitaría la anulación del resultado por supuestas irregularidades electorales, pero su Partido Liberal declaró el lunes que reconocía la victoria de Lula. Sigue sin estar claro cómo logró Bolsonaro salir del país mientras pesaba sobre él una orden del Supremo Tribunal Federal (la corte suprema local) que le daba un plazo de 24 horas para entregar sus pasaportes. Un alto cargo de la Policía Federal brasileña dijo que Bolsonaro no abandonó el país a través de ningún punto migratorio oficial. El 'influencer' de derecha Paulo Figueiredo, que oficia como un portavoz no oficial de la familia Bolsonaro, se negó a responder a preguntas sobre el paradero de Bolsonaro. "Tras meses de intenso trabajo que se ha visto frustrado injustamente, no estoy de humor para hablar con la prensa", dijo en un mensaje. "Si tengo algún comentario que hacer sobre cualquier asunto, me pondré en contacto". Eduardo Bolsonaro, el hermano menor de Flávio que vive en Estados Unidos, dijo antes de las elecciones que una derrota electoral le obligaría a marcharse del país. "Si mi hermano no gana, estoy a favor de que se marche del país", dijo al podcaster Steven Crowder el 23 de octubre.

item.title: Rendimientos en EEUU suben mientras los inversores esperan la decisión de la Fed
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron ligeramente el martes, mientras los inversionistas sopesaban las perspectivas de alzas de las tasas de interés, antes de la decisión de la Reserva Federal del miércoles.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subieron ligeramente el martes, mientras los inversionistas sopesaban las perspectivas de alzas de las tasas de interés, antes de la decisión de la Reserva Federal del miércoles. La actividad bursátil fue tranquila tras la reciente volatilidad de los mercados. Los precios de los bonos del Tesoro habían subido la semana pasada, lo que hizo bajar los rendimientos, ya que las preocupaciones sobre la sostenibilidad del auge de la inteligencia artificial (IA) provocó una caída de las acciones y aumentó el atractivo de los bonos como un refugio. El rendimiento de referencia a 10 años había anotado el jueves pasado su mayor caída en un solo día en casi cuatro años, a medida que las acciones bajaban. El martes subió ligeramente, pero se mantuvo en menos de la cota del 5%. El mercado está a la espera de la conclusión de la reunión de la Fed, el miércoles. Se espera que el banco central mantenga las tasas de interés sin cambios cuando anuncie su decisión de política monetaria, pero los inversionistas no creen que una pausa en las subidas de tasas vaya a durar mucho, dadas la persistente preocupación sobre la inflación. Una subasta de bonos a cinco años de 70.000 millones de dólares arrojó resultados dispares. Tuvo un rendimiento ligeramente superior a la tasa indicada en el momento de presentación de ofertas, lo que indica que los inversores exigieron un extra para absorber la oferta. El ratio de cobertura, otro indicador de la demanda, fue ligeramente superior al de la última subasta. "El mercado está lidiando con la oferta y con las reuniones de la Fed y el BCE esta semana. Probablemente ambos bancos centrales adoptarán un tono restrictivo", dijo Tom di Galoma, director general de Mischler Financial Group. "No creo que los operadores estén asumiendo muchos riesgos". El rendimiento del bono del Tesoro estadounidense a 10 años de referencia subió 0,2 puntos básicos, al 4,988%, mientras que el del papel a 30 años cerró sin cambios en 5,301%. El rendimiento de las notas del Tesoro estadounidense a dos años , que suele evolucionar en consonancia con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, avanzó 2,4 puntos básicos, al 4,735%. La diferencia entre los rendimientos de las notas del Tesoro a 2 y a 10 años , que se considera un indicador de las expectativas económicas, era de 25,1 puntos básicos, la más baja en un mes.

item.title: Canada, UAE sign trade deal as Carney seeks new trading partners
item.description: Canada and the United Arab Emirates signed a comprehensive trade deal on Tuesday to lower barriers between the two economies and boost investment, the governments said, as Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to expand trade and investment ties at a time of tension with the United States.
item.dc:creator: Promit Mukherjee, Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Canada and the United Arab Emirates signed a comprehensive trade deal on Tuesday to lower barriers between the two economies and boost investment, the governments said, as Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to expand trade and investment ties at a time of tension with the United States. Carney and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan presided over the signing of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), which aims to cut tariffs, reduce red tape and improve market access for businesses in both countries. Carney has vowed to double Canada's non-US trade over the next decade as President Donald Trump's tariffs have rippled through Canada's economy. Subsequent attempts for a deal with Washington have broken down, and that has pushed Carney to aggressively pursue trade pacts with countries from the Asia Pacific to Europe and Middle East. "Once fully implemented, the CEPA will reduce or eliminate tariffs on over 99% of current Canadian exports to the UAE. That means new markets for Canadian farmers growing pulses and canola, for manufacturers of industrial machinery and power generation equipment, for our world-class aerospace sector, and other Canadian innovators," The Prime Minister's Office said in a statement. "The agreement will also address non-tariff barriers, create a more predictable environment for trade and investment, and expand market access for Canadian goods and services, including in the industrial, agricultural, forest, fish and seafood, environmental, and engineering sectors," it said, adding CEPA is expected to enter into force in 2027. The two countries also signed preliminary agreements on energy, diplomatic and defence cooperation. "We see considerable potential for our private sector, whether through improved market access for our exporters or access to investment opportunities in high-growth sectors such as logistics, communications, advanced technology and manufacturing – all of which will support our pursuit of a resilient, diversified and globally connected economy,” UAE's Foreign Trade Minister Thani Al Zeyoudi said in a statement. He signed the CEPA deal with his Canadian counterpart Maninder Sidhu. UAE is the largest Middle Eastern market for Canadian exports and is a big buyer of Canadian motor vehicles and parts, and machinery. Two-way trade between the countries was worth C$3.5 billion ($2.48 billion) last year. It has been growing at 10% annually for the last few years, according to a government data. The UAE last year also committed up to in Canada. The signing is the last step before Canada’s Parliament can ratify the agreement, a Canadian government source said.

item.title: Monedas cierran mixtas, real brasileño se recupera tras desplome en la jornada previa
item.description: Las monedas de América Latina anotaron un desempeño dispar el martes, en una jornada en que el real brasileño se recuperó de parte del desplome de la ronda previa, mientras la atención del mercado se centraba en el inicio de la reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Froilan Romero
item.content:encoded: Las monedas de América Latina anotaron un desempeño dispar el martes, en una jornada en que el real brasileño se recuperó de parte del desplome de la ronda previa, mientras la atención del mercado se centraba en el inicio de la reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos. * Los activos brasileños se hundieron el lunes debido al triunfo del presidente de izquierda Luiz Inácio Lula Da Silva en el balotaje ante Flávio Bolsonaro, favorito de los mercados. * La Fed mantendría sin cambios las tasas de interés el miércoles, y el mercado espera pistas sobre si podría haber un alza en diciembre. Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, los operadores ven una probabilidad del 80% de un aumento de tipos a fines de año. * El real brasileño se apreció un 1,07%, a 5,3488 unidades por dólar tras hundirse más de un 8% el lunes. En tanto, el índice Bovespa (.BVSP) de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo bajó un 0,44%, a 175.831,92 puntos, luego que el lunes anotó su mayor caída diaria desde marzo de 2020. * El peso mexicano cotizaba cerca del cierre en 18,6743 unidades por dólar, con una caída del 0,59%. El principal índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, subía un 0,32%, a 69.703,62 unidades, después de tres sesiones de pérdidas. * Los inversionistas mantenían la mirada puesta en la temporada de resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre, que concluye esta semana. * En Argentina, el peso mayorista se apreció el 0,16% a 1.538,5 por dólar , aunque en su apertura anotó el piso récord de 1.550 unidades, ante un banco central (BCRA) que el lunes cortó una racha de 19 días consecutivos con compras de divisas para reforzar sus reservas internacionales. * La autoridad monetaria tampoco absorbió divisas el martes en medio de un mercado cambiario controlado. * En tanto, el índice bursátil MSCI Merval (.MMXMRVLGA) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires cayó un 2,24%, y los bonos públicos extrabursátiles promediaban un retroceso del 0,6%. * El peso chileno , se apreció un 1,12%, a 981,80/982,10 por dólar, apoyado en un alza en los precios del cobre, el mayor envío del país. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , escaló un 1,80%, a 10.766,07 unidades. * El peso colombiano cerró con caída de un 0,56% a 3.147,40 unidades por dólar, luego de tres jornadas de ganancias; en tanto que en la bolsa el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) subió un 0,07% a 2.506,69 puntos. * La moneda peruana, el sol , se depreció un 0,23% a 3,4490/3,4510 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) mejoraba un 1,14% a 1.528,86 puntos.

item.title: Wall Street cierra al alza gracias al renovado impulso de la IA
item.description: Un repunte tecnológico impulsado por la inteligencia artificial llevó a las bolsas estadounidenses a cerrar al alza el martes, a medida que la temporada de presentación de resultados del tercer trimestre cobraba impulso y mientras la Reserva Federal se reunía para celebrar su penúltima reunión del año.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: Un repunte tecnológico impulsado por la inteligencia artificial llevó a las bolsas estadounidenses a cerrar al alza el martes, a medida que la temporada de presentación de resultados del tercer trimestre cobraba impulso y mientras la Reserva Federal se reunía para celebrar su penúltima reunión del año. El Nasdaq, con gran presencia tecnológica, encabezó las subidas. El revuelo en torno a los detalles de la inminente salida a bolsa de Anthropic contribuyó a impulsar las acciones de las empresas de semiconductores (.SOX) por tercera sesión consecutiva. La creciente preocupación por la viabilidad del gasto financiado con deuda, en un contexto de subida de los costos de financiación, ha lastrado el sector de la IA este mes. El índice Philadelphia SE Semiconductor, aunque se sitúa más de un 20% por debajo de su máximo histórico de cierre del 22 de junio, ha superado al mercado en general este año. Para financiar su expansión en el ámbito de la IA, Meta (META.O) aumentó su mayor ronda de financiación de capital hasta la fecha a 97.500 millones de dólares, lo que provocó una caída de las acciones de la empresa matriz de Facebook. "(La noticia sobre Anthropic) parece estar provocando un pequeño repunte de alivio en las acciones del sector de la IA, especialmente en las de semiconductores", dijo Chuck Carlson, presidente ejecutivo de Horizon Investment Services, refiriéndose a las acciones de fabricantes de chips. "Esas acciones se han visto muy castigadas en las últimas semanas y probablemente ya era hora de que se recuperaran". Los datos económicos mostraron un aumento de los nuevos pedidos de computadores y equipos periféricos, lo que respalda la idea de un fuerte gasto relacionado con la IA. Se espera que Microsoft (MSFT.O) y Alphabet (GOOGL.O) publiquen sus resultados el miércoles, mientras que Amazon.com lo hará el jueves. La Fed se reunió el martes para celebrar su reunión de política monetaria de octubre, de la que se espera ampliamente que culmine con la decisión de mantener sin cambios la tasa de interés objetivo de los fondos federales en el rango del 3,75% al 4%, reservando su segunda subida de tasas del año para su última reunión en diciembre, según la herramienta FedWatch de CME. "Parece haber más confianza en que la Fed no va a tomar ninguna medida en esta reunión, en parte porque el martes hay elecciones", añadió Carlson. "Probablemente haya al menos cierto alivio al saber que la situación de las tasas no va a obstaculizar un repunte". Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) subió 46,28 puntos, o un 0,60%, a 7.723,05 unidades, mientras que el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) ganó 309,69 puntos, o un 1,18%, a 26.479,08. El Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) avanzó 25,60 puntos, o un 0,05%, a 52.387,18 unidades.

item.title: AI financing driving private credit growth as refinancing risks rise, Moody’s says
item.description: High levels of borrowing to fund AI infrastructure is expanding private credit beyond traditional corporate lending, but a wave of loans coming due in the next few years could leave weaker borrowers struggling to refinance, Moody's Ratings said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: High levels of borrowing to fund AI infrastructure is expanding private credit beyond traditional corporate lending, but a wave of loans coming due in the next few years could leave weaker borrowers struggling to refinance, Moody's Ratings said on Tuesday.
